stories.title: Automated Incident Response via GitOps PRs
stories.story: Given an incident has been classified and assigned a runbook, When the autonomous triage triggers the remediation workflow, Then a GitOps pull request is automatically created containing the runbook-specific changes
acceptance_criteria: Incident classification triggers automated remediation workflow
Runbook-specific changes are rendered as a Git diff
GitOps PR is created with proper title, description, and labels
PR references the incident ID in the commit message
PR creation is idempotent (no duplicate PRs for same incident+runbook combination)

tasks.description: Design and implement RemediationWorkflow engine that receives classified incidents and maps them to runbooks
Implement Git provider abstraction layer (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket) for PR creation
Build PR templating engine that renders runbook changes as Git diffs with incident context

stories.title: Declarative Runbook Definitions Stored in Git
stories.story: Given an SRE author has created a runbook definition in YAML, When the runbook is committed to the runbooks repository, Then the runbook is validated against the runbook schema and the runbook contains: trigger conditions, remediation steps, rollback procedure, approval requirements, and severity mapping
acceptance_criteria: Runbook YAML schema is defined and versioned
Schema validation occurs on commit (via webhook or CI)
Runbook contains: triggers, remediation steps, rollback procedure, approval requirements, severity mapping
Invalid runbooks are rejected with clear error messages
Runbook registry is queryable via API

tasks.description: Define and version the runbook YAML schema (JSON Schema / CUE)
Implement schema validation service that runs on commit hooks and CI pipelines
Build runbook registry API for querying and indexing runbooks

stories.title: Audit Trail and Rollback via Git History
stories.story: Given a remediation action has been executed via a merged PR, When an auditor queries the remediation history for a specific incident, Then the complete git history shows: who approved, what changed, when it was deployed, and the rollback commit
acceptance_criteria: Every remediation PR creates a verifiable audit trail in Git history
Audit query returns: approver identity, diff summary, deployment timestamp, rollback commit SHA
Rollback is a single-click operation that creates a revert PR
Audit trail is immutable (signed commits, branch protection)
API endpoint exposes audit history for compliance queries

tasks.description: Implement audit trail data model and storage (Git-referenced metadata)
Build audit query API with filtering by incident, date range, approver, and service
Implement one-click rollback via automated revert PR creation

stories.title: Policy-as-Code for Remediation Approval Gates
stories.story: Given a remediation PR has been created, When the PR is evaluated by the policy engine, Then the PR is tagged with required approvers based on: severity level, affected service, and environment (prod/staging/dev)
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine evaluates every remediation PR via webhook
Policies are defined as code (Rego/OPA) and stored in a policies directory
Required approvers are dynamically assigned based on severity, service, environment
P0 production changes require 2+ approvers including an SRE lead
Policy violations block PR merge with clear rejection reasons

tasks.description: Integrate OPA/Rego policy engine and define policy data model
Write Rego policies for approval gates: severity-based, service-based, environment-based
Build webhook handler that evaluates PRs and tags with required approvers

stories.title: Real-Time Cloud Cost Anomaly Detection per Region per Provider
stories.story: Given cost telemetry is being ingested from AWS/GCP/Azure for each region (EU, US), When a cost metric deviates beyond the dynamic threshold (e.g., >3 standard deviations from trailing 7-day baseline), Then an anomaly alert is created and the FinOps engine triggers an optimization scan
acceptance_criteria: Cost telemetry ingestion from AWS (Cost Explorer API), GCP (Billing API), Azure (Cost Management API)
Per-region, per-service cost baseline computed from trailing 7-day window
Dynamic thresholding using rolling statistics (mean, std dev, z-score)
Anomaly alert triggers automated optimization scan
Anomalies are viewable in dashboard with drill-down to provider/region/service

tasks.description: Implement cloud cost telemetry ingestion pipeline with provider adapters (AWS, GCP, Azure)
Build anomaly detection engine with dynamic thresholding (z-score, rolling window statistics)
Create anomaly alerting and notification pipeline (PagerDuty, Slack, Webhook)

stories.title: Automated Cost Optimization Recommendations with Projected ROI
stories.story: Given a cost anomaly or a scheduled optimization scan has been triggered, When the FinOps engine analyzes the cost data across all providers and regions, Then it generates optimization recommendations showing: resource ID, current cost, recommended action, projected monthly savings, implementation complexity, and ROI confidence score
acceptance_criteria: Optimization scan is triggered by anomaly or on a schedule (daily/weekly)
Recommendations include: resource ID, current cost, action, projected savings, complexity, ROI score
Recommendation types: right-sizing, reserved instances, spot instances, storage tiering, unused resource elimination
ROI calculation includes implementation cost vs projected 30/60/90-day savings
Recommendations are stored and queryable via API

tasks.description: Build optimization analysis engine with recommendation generators for each provider
Implement ROI projection calculator with confidence scoring
Create recommendations API and storage layer

stories.title: Showback/Show-Charge Reporting per SRE Team per Service
stories.story: Given cost allocation tags are configured per SRE team and service, When the monthly billing cycle completes, Then a showback report is generated per team showing: total cost, cost by provider, cost by region, cost trend over last 3 months, and top 5 cost drivers
acceptance_criteria: Cost allocation tags are configurable per team, service, and environment
Monthly showback report is auto-generated on billing cycle completion
Report shows: total cost, provider breakdown, regional breakdown, 3-month trend, top 5 cost drivers
Reports are exportable as PDF, CSV, and viewable in dashboard
Showback data is queryable via API with team and date filters

tasks.description: Implement cost allocation tag management and ingestion
Build monthly showback report generator with multi-dimensional breakdowns
Create report export service (PDF, CSV) and dashboard widgets

stories.title: Cost vs. Reliability Trade-off Visualization Dashboard
stories.story: Given the SRE team has configured their reliability SLOs and cost budgets, When a user navigates to the trade-off dashboard, Then they see a scatter plot of all services comparing: monthly cost (x-axis), error budget burn rate (y-axis), and risk quadrant (under-funded, optimal, over-engineered, at-risk)
acceptance_criteria: SLO and cost budget configurations are stored per service
Scatter plot renders with monthly cost on x-axis and error budget burn rate on y-axis
Risk quadrants are clearly labeled: under-funded, optimal, over-engineered, at-risk
Clicking a service point shows detailed SLO and cost breakdown
Dashboard supports date range filtering and export

tasks.description: Implement SLO and cost budget configuration storage and API
Build trade-off analytics engine (cost vs error budget burn rate computation)
Create scatter plot dashboard with risk quadrant visualization and drill-down

stories.title: AI-Powered Incident Triage for Severity and Ownership Classification
stories.story: Given an alert or incident notification arrives from any monitoring source, When the triage agent processes the incident, Then it classifies severity (P0/P1/P2/P3/P4) with a confidence score and it assigns ownership to the appropriate SRE team based on service ownership mapping
acceptance_criteria: Ingests alerts from Prometheus, Datadog, Grafana, CloudWatch, and generic webhooks
Severity classification with confidence score (P0-P4)
Owner assignment based on service ownership mapping and on-call schedule
Classification accuracy >= 90% for P0/P1 (measured against human review)
API returns classification result with confidence, rationale, and alternative assignments

tasks.description: Build alert ingestion pipeline with multiple source adapters (Prometheus, Datadog, Grafana, CloudWatch, webhook)
Implement LLM-based severity classifier with confidence scoring and fallback heuristics
Build service ownership mapping and on-call schedule integration for team assignment

stories.title: Automated Root Cause Analysis Suggestions
stories.story: Given an incident has been classified by the triage agent, When the RCA engine analyzes the incident context (logs, metrics, traces, recent changes), Then it produces a ranked list of likely root causes with supporting evidence and confidence scores
acceptance_criteria: RCA engine consumes logs, metrics, traces, and recent change events
Produces ranked list of root causes with evidence snippets and confidence scores
Integrates with OpenTelemetry for trace analysis
Integrates with Git history for recent change correlation
RCA results are stored with the incident record for post-mortem analysis

tasks.description: Implement context collector service (logs, metrics, traces, Git changes)
Build RCA analysis engine with ranking and evidence extraction
Create RCA storage and API for incident correlation

stories.title: Self-Healing Runbook Execution via Autonomous Agents
stories.story: Given an incident has been classified with an automatable runbook available, When the self-healing agent matches the incident to a runbook with confidence > 90%, Then the agent creates a GitOps remediation PR automatically, executes dry-run first, and reports results back to the incident timeline
acceptance_criteria: Self-healing agent matches incidents to runbooks with confidence scoring
Automated GitOps PR creation for matched runbooks (confidence > 90%)
Dry-run execution before actual remediation
Results reported back to incident timeline
Agent provides rollback plan in the PR description

tasks.description: Implement runbook matching engine (incident-to-runbook classifier)
Build self-healing agent orchestrator with dry-run capability
Integrate with incident timeline for result reporting and rollback plan generation

stories.title: Escalation Logic with Human-in-the-Loop for Critical Decisions
stories.story: Given an incident requires escalation (P0, or self-healing failure, or low-confidence classification), When the escalation engine evaluates the escalation policy, Then it pages the on-call engineer with full incident context, classification details, and suggested remediation steps
acceptance_criteria: Escalation policy is configurable as code (JSON/YAML/Rego)
Escalation triggers: P0 incidents, self-healing failure, classification confidence < 70%
On-call engineer is paged with full incident context and suggested steps
Escalation supports multi-tier: engineer → team lead → SRE manager
Escalation and response are tracked in the incident timeline

tasks.description: Design and implement escalation policy engine with configurable rules
Build paging integration (PagerDuty, OpsGenie, Slack) with incident context payload
Implement multi-tier escalation logic and incident timeline tracking

stories.title: Offline-Capable SRE Dashboard with Local-First Architecture
stories.story: Given an SRE engineer has network connectivity, When they open the SRE dashboard, Then the dashboard loads data from the local-first store (IndexedDB/SQLite in browser) with cloud sync as background, and When the engineer loses connectivity, Then the dashboard continues to function with locally cached data and queues changes for sync
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard loads from local store first (offline-first), syncs with cloud in background
All core features work offline: viewing incidents, runbooks, service health
Changes made offline are queued and synced when connectivity is restored
Sync conflicts are resolved using CRDT-based strategies
User sees clear connectivity status indicator and sync progress

tasks.description: Set up local-first data layer with IndexedDB/SQLite and CRDT integration
Build offline-capable dashboard UI with connectivity-aware rendering
Implement background sync engine with conflict resolution and queue management

stories.title: Local-First Runbook Authoring and Versioning
stories.story: Given an SRE engineer is editing a runbook offline, When they make changes to the YAML runbook definition, Then changes are stored locally using CRDTs for conflict-free data types, and the local version is synced to Git when connectivity is restored
acceptance_criteria: Runbook editor works fully offline with YAML validation
Changes use CRDT (Y.js) for conflict-free concurrent editing
Local changes are auto-synced to Git repository when online
Multiple engineers can edit the same runbook with automatic merge
Version history is preserved locally and in Git

tasks.description: Build YAML runbook editor with offline support and real-time validation
Integrate CRDT (Y.js) for conflict-free concurrent editing of runbooks
Implement Git sync bridge that converts CRDT changes to Git commits

stories.title: P2P Sync Between SRE Team Member Workspaces
stories.story: Given multiple SRE engineers are working in the same region on the same incident, When one engineer updates the incident timeline or runbook locally, Then the change is synced peer-to-peer to other online team members in real-time via WebRTC
acceptance_criteria: P2P sync uses WebRTC for direct browser-to-browser connections
Changes are synced in real-time across online team members
P2P sync works without cloud backend (LAN-only mode)
Sync includes: incident timeline updates, runbook edits, annotations
Connection status and sync state are visible per team member

tasks.description: Implement WebRTC signaling and P2P connection management
Build CRDT-based P2P sync protocol for incident timeline and runbook data
Create team presence UI showing member online status and sync state

stories.title: Progressive Sync to Cloud Backend When Online
stories.story: Given an SRE engineer's local workspace has accumulated changes while offline, When connectivity is restored, Then the workspace progressively syncs changes to the cloud backend in order of priority: incident timeline updates first, then runbook changes, then configuration changes, and sync progress is displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria: Sync order prioritization: incident timeline > runbook changes > configuration changes
Sync progress is visible with per-item status (pending, syncing, synced, failed)
Failed syncs are retried with exponential backoff
Sync is bandwidth-aware (progressive, chunked uploads)
User can pause/resume sync and view sync history

tasks.description: Design and implement priority-based sync queue with ordering
Build progressive sync engine with chunked uploads, retry logic, and bandwidth awareness
Create sync progress UI with per-item status visibility and pause/resume controls
